# Global Public Surface — Phase Two Critique

The Awtsmoos does not reveal more by throwing every internal corridor onto the street;
Awtsmoos.com should expose complete products, not tests, debug fossils, or implementation fragments beneath the feet.

## Critique of naive catalog expansion

A filesystem directory is not automatically a public app. Internal subroutes, test harnesses, old copies, generated viewers, and temporary pages can all contain `index.html` without representing user-facing products. Therefore the catalog must be built from evidence: canonical top-level product entries plus explicitly productized nested entries.

A catalog can also become cluttered even when complete. The visible layer should remain simple and scan-friendly. Deep metadata belongs in collapsible details or manifests, not permanently expanded cards.

## Better discovery rules

- `/apps/<slug>/index.html` is a strong public-app signal unless the slug is test/debug/old/tmp/internal/generated-only.
- `/games/<slug>/index.html` is a strong public-game signal under the same exclusions.
- Nested product routes are public only when already referenced by catalog/manifests/navigation or clearly packaged as standalone products.
- Existing explicit catalog manifests beat heuristics when present.
- Every candidate must resolve to an actual entry file.
- Canonical route normalization removes trailing duplicate variants.
- Missing public products should be added through the catalog's existing data model, not hardcoded into unrelated markup.

## UI danger map

The next runtime probe should prioritize fixed-position overlays, modal sheets, hard widths >=480px, min-width >=390px, `100vw` controls inside padded parents, high z-index stacks, and hover-only animated controls. A static signal earns inspection, not mutation.
